name: All Fours (Yorkshire)
description: West Yorkshire All Fours is a cherished pub league tradition in Northern England, particularly centered in the Heavy Woollen District (Batley, Heckmondwike). Unlike the classic game, it uses a 'Pitch' start with no turn-up card and features unique regional etiquette such as the 'First Trick Face Up' rule.

content.text: West Yorkshire All Fours is a cherished pub league tradition in Northern England, particularly centered in the Heavy Woollen District (Batley, Heckmondwike). Unlike the classic game, it uses a 'Pitch' start with no turn-up card and features unique regional etiquette such as the 'First Trick Face Up' rule.
Rooted in the industrial heartlands of Yorkshire, the game evolved alongside the textile mills. It became a formalized league sport in the mid-20th century.
4 players in two partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
Standard deck, All Fours pegging board (traditionally to 11 points).
Each player receives 6 cards in batches of 3. No card is turned for trump.

items.text: Heckmondwike League Standard: Played to 15 points instead of 11 to allow for longer, more strategic matches.
